games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence is a correct second conditional?
choices: If the bay was cleaner, more fish will return.
If the bay were cleaner, more fish would return.
If the bay is cleaner, more fish would return.
If the bay would be cleaner, more fish returned.
rounds.answer: If the bay were cleaner, more fish would return.
rounds.explanation: The second conditional imagines the present: if plus past ('were'), then would plus the base verb, as in Units 3 and 4.

rounds.prompt: In 'The officials tried to play down the pollution report', what does 'play down' mean?
choices: to refuse to talk about something ever again
to make something seem less important
to practise before a serious match
to celebrate a result loudly
rounds.answer: to make something seem less important
rounds.explanation: Play down means to minimise: the officials wanted the report to seem smaller than it was, a phrasal verb from the Unit 7 pattern set.

rounds.prompt: Choose the missing word from 'Review text 3': The park wardens hoped the new signs would ______ visitors from leaving the marked trails.
choices: commemorate
exult
deter
falter
rounds.answer: deter
rounds.explanation: Review text 3 says the wardens hoped the new signs would deter visitors from leaving the marked trails; deter means to make someone decide not to act.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: According to Review text 1, what did the Fact-Checker's Toolkit train readers to do before sharing a story?
choices: To ask five questions first: who wrote this, when was it written, what evidence supports it, is it plausible, and who benefits if I believe it.
The movement started small, stayed visible and handed every neighbour a job worth doing, so results like new bins and clean-ups kept it growing.
Two days later another essay appeared by someone else, then more followed, printed by hand and passed under desks until a patient, systematic network had formed.
rounds.answer: To ask five questions first: who wrote this, when was it written, what evidence supports it, is it plausible, and who benefits if I believe it.
rounds.explanation: Review text 1 says the Fact-Checker's Toolkit handed you five steady questions to slow the race to share: who wrote this, when was it written, what evidence supports it, is it plausible, and who benefits if I believe it.

rounds.prompt: What single lesson does Review text 3 draw from both Marka's shoreline and the Simien Highlands expedition?
choices: The movement started small, stayed visible and handed every neighbour a job worth doing, so results like new bins and clean-ups kept it growing.
Language is power, and power demands evidence, fairness and craft.
Places recover when people take patient responsibility: bring counts rather than impressions, compare fairly and refuse to rush past the evidence.
rounds.answer: Places recover when people take patient responsibility: bring counts rather than impressions, compare fairly and refuse to rush past the evidence.
rounds.explanation: The text says: Places recover when people take patient responsibility: bring counts rather than impressions, compare fairly and refuse to rush past the evidence.

rounds.prompt: What does Review text 5 name as the one steady lesson running through all nine units of the year?
choices: He admitted he could not prove it, so he refused to accuse anyone; he called the behaviour repugnant and led his cast to rewrite and perform without the mask.
Language is power, and power demands evidence, fairness and craft.
Nadir's pitch was slick and polished but thin on evidence, while the winners rehearsed, spoke with calm authority and brought working results, so proof beat polish.
rounds.answer: Language is power, and power demands evidence, fairness and craft.
rounds.explanation: In the paragraph that looks back over the whole road, Review text 5 sums up nine units in one sentence: language is power, and power demands evidence, fairness and craft.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: The mayor said, 'The first units will be installed by December.' Which reported version is correct?
choices: The mayor said that the first units would be installed by December.
The mayor said that the first units will been installed by December.
The mayor said that the first units would being installed by December.
The mayor said that the first units are install by December.
rounds.answer: The mayor said that the first units would be installed by December.
rounds.explanation: Reported speech steps 'will be installed' back to 'would be installed', keeping the passive intact, as practised with Unit 5's story.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the past perfect correctly?
choices: By morning, a network of writers was form at Kambazi School.
By morning, a network of writers has formed at Kambazi School.
By morning, a network of writers had forming at Kambazi School.
By morning, a network of writers had formed at Kambazi School.
rounds.answer: By morning, a network of writers had formed at Kambazi School.
rounds.explanation: 'By morning' sets a past deadline, so the earlier event takes had plus the past participle: had formed, as in Unit 7.

rounds.prompt: Imani ______ her closing story since the opening round of the StoryForge. Which form completes the sentence?
choices: has been shaping
has shaped being
is been shaping
have been shaping
rounds.answer: has been shaping
rounds.explanation: 'Since the opening round' measures unfinished duration, so the present perfect continuous fits: has been shaping, from Unit 8.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: Which review word from Unit 1 means 'using few words to say something clearly'?
choices: temperate
concise
gullible
plausible
rounds.answer: concise
rounds.explanation: Concise writing keeps only the words that earn their place, like the questioning club's one-line rule in Unit 1.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence compares two climbers correctly?
choices: Zara climbed more carefully than the lone climber.
Zara climbed most carefully than the lone climber.
Zara climbed more carefully of the lone climber.
Zara climbed the most carefully than the lone climber.
rounds.answer: Zara climbed more carefully than the lone climber.
rounds.explanation: Two actions compared take a comparative adverb with 'than': more carefully than. Superlatives need three or more.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence is in the present continuous passive?
choices: New bins are affixed along the beach paths every season.
Volunteers are affixing new bins along the beach paths.
New bins are being affixed along the beach paths.
New bins will be affixed along the beach paths soon.
rounds.answer: New bins are being affixed along the beach paths.
rounds.explanation: The present continuous passive is are or is plus being plus a past participle, as in Unit 3's clean-up scenes.
